title: Maximum Sum Queries
summary: Given arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, and queries where each query specifies xi and yi, find the maximum value of nums1[j] + nums2[j] for all j where nums1[j] is at least xi and nums2[j] is at least yi.
statement: Given arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, and queries where each query specifies xi and yi, find the maximum value of nums1[j] + nums2[j] for all j where nums1[j] is at least xi and nums2[j] is at least yi. If no such j exists, return -1 for each query. Return an array of answers corresponding to each query.
constraints: Point i has coordinates nums1[i] and nums2[i] and value nums1[i]+nums2[i].
For query [x,y], consider points whose first coordinate is at least x and second is at least y.
Return the maximum point value for every query, or -1 when no point qualifies.
reference_solution:
def maximum_sum_queries(nums1,nums2,queries):
    values=sorted(set(nums2+[y for _,y in queries]));size=len(values);tree=[-1]*(size+1)
    def update(index,value):
        index=size-index
        while index<=size:tree[index]=max(tree[index],value);index+=index&-index
    def lookup(index):
        index=size-index;answer=-1
        while index>0:answer=max(answer,tree[index]);index-=index&-index
        return answer
    from bisect import bisect_left
    points=sorted(zip(nums1,nums2),reverse=True);ordered=sorted(enumerate(queries),key=lambda item:item[1][0],reverse=True)
    answer=[-1]*len(queries);point=0
    for query_index,(x,y) in ordered:
        while point<len(points) and points[point][0]>=x:
            first,second=points[point];update(bisect_left(values,second),first+second);point+=1
        answer[query_index]=lookup(bisect_left(values,y))
    return answer
